content.text: Indian mythology has bestowed Ayurveda with a divine aura and stature. Indians consider their premises and precepts as a direct ‘Gift from the Gods’. The roots of Ayurveda in Kerala are pretty deep. The earliest proponents of Ayurveda were Charaka, Sushruta and Vagbhata. Among them, for Ayurveda in Kerala, it is Vagbhata who is widely regarded as the promoter of Ayurveda. So, BAMS is a trendy course in Kerala. There are 18 medical colleges that provide the BAMS course. The general admission criteria are the same as the other states. In this article, we will cover everything related to BAMS admission in Kerala, including Top colleges, fees, eligibility, and more.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission in Kerala Overview

content.text: It is mandatory to qualify for NEET-UG and participate in Ayush counselling for admission to the BAMS course. The Kerala AYUSH counselling is conducted by the Commissioner of Entrance Examinations (CEE) . There are a total of 1096 BAMS seats in the state. There are 5 government colleges responsible for 346 seats, and the other 13 private colleges take up 750 students. Kerala BAMS counselling happens once a year. The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. All the BAMS seats in Kerala are offered under both the State Quota and All India Quota. The eligibility for BAMS admission in Kerala is stated below.

sections.heading: Eligibility for BAMS Course in Kerala

content.text: NEET is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. Apart from the qualifying exam, students must meet certain requirements for admission. The eligibility for the BAMS course in Kerala requires the students to meet the following criteria.

items: Securing a qualifying score in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test(NEET UG) is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. NEET is a national-level entrance exam that is conducted by NTA every year.
Candidates must complete 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB) as core subjects.

The minimum marks required for BAMS admission can vary depending on the college and reservation category. Generally, a minimum aggregate of 50% in PCB subjects is mandatory for the general category. However, some colleges might have a higher cut-off percentage. SC, ST, and OBC categories have lower mark requirements, which is 40% aggregate marks.
Candidates should be aged over 17 years at the time of admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Kerala

content.text: The step-by-step procedure for BAMS admission in Kerala is given below. All admissions, regardless to the private or government colleges, occur according to the CEE.
Step 1: Appear in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test and score above the cut-off marks for admission in the BAMS course.
Step 2: Go to the Kerala AYUSH counselling website and complete your registration. Fill out the application form by inputting all of your personal and academic information.
Step 3: Complete the document verification procedure. Carry all the prescribed documents, both in photocopies and originals.
Step 4: Take part in the Kerala State Counselling. Provide your preferences and fill choices of colleges.
Step 5: Seat allotment occurs based on NEET Ayush rank, options filled, reservation criteria, etc. You can view your seat allotment status on the counselling portal.
Step 6: Once allotted a seat, report to the college to finalise your candidature. It requires paying the admission fees necessary for confirmation.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Admission

content.text: Below is the list of documents required for BAMS admission in Kerala. These documents are necessary to go ahead with the admission procedure. Candidates have to verify these documents before the counselling procedure and get them to the college after counselling for further documentation:

items: 10th Certificate (Matriculation Certificate).
12th Certificate (Plus Two Certificate).
Birth Certificate.
Allotment Memo by AYUSH.
Transfer Certificate.
Migration Certificate.
Aadhar card.
Community Certificate.
NEET Admit Card.
Nativity Certificate.
Fee Receipt (AYUSH)
Fitness Certificate.
Passport size photos – No. 6

content.text: Note: It is advisable to keep 2 or 3 photocopies of the documents to avoid any inconvenience during admission.

content.text: The course fees for BAMS are different depending on the college type. While the private colleges charge more, the government colleges are well-known for their good infrastructure and good placement record. Still, the government colleges are a lot cheaper compared to the fees of the private ones. Here, the overview of the fee range is given for both the private and the government colleges. sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
What are the fees of a BAMS private college in Kerala?

content.text: Private colleges in Kerala charge a fee of INR 1,90,000/- to INR 4 lacs per year for the BAMS course.

sections.heading: What are the eligibility criteria for BAMS admission in Kerala?

content.text: The eligibility for BAMS course in Kerala is that a candidate must have passed the two-year Pre-University or Plus Two or 12th examination or Intermediate or equivalent with Science subjects, obtaining at least 50% aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry and Biology. The candidate also has to be 17 years of age as on 31st December of the current year.

sections.heading: How can I get admission to BAMS in Kerala?

content.text: After qualifying NEET UG, fill out the application form and submit it online on the website of CEE . Follow the steps to take BAMS admission in Kerala.

sections.heading: How many BAMS colleges are there in Kerala?

content.text: There are a total of 18 colleges for BAMS admission in Kerala. Among them, 5 are government colleges and the rest of 13 are private ones.

sections.heading: Is there any entrance test for BAMS admission in Kerala?

content.text: Yes, for taking admission in BAMS course, all the students must qualify the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. NEET UG is considered the sole entrance test for BAMS admission all over India.

sections.heading: Which is the Kerala BAMS counselling authority?

content.text: The Commissioner of Entrance Examinations (CEE) is the Kerala BAMS counselling authority.

sections.heading: What are the BAMS course fees in Kerala?

content.text: The BAMS course fees in Kerala range from INR 12,000/- to INR 4.5 lacs. It solely depends on the colleges. The fees are taken every year.

sections.heading: Can other state students apply for BAMS admission in Kerala?

content.text: Yes, students from other state can apply for BAMS admission in Kerala under the All India Quota (AIQ).
